title: Is Ford Stock A Buy?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether Ford is a buy after a decade of policy whiplash: forced into EVs with no competitive advantage, then the EV mandate scrapped, plus tariffs hitting a supply chain spanning Canada, the US and Mexico. Policy has now turned in Ford's favour - the F-150 Lightning is scrapped in favour of the ICE F-150, tariffs are trending down after Supreme Court rulings, and friendlier Canada relations may cut them further. Wall Street forecasts 28% EPS growth over the next several years, helped by rising average selling prices. But autos are never very lucrative: the operating margin is just 1.8% now (it peaked around 2022 when shortages pushed prices above MSRP), and returning to low-to-mid single digits would be a win. Valuation compensates: a forward P/E of just 6, less than a quarter of forward EPS estimates. His DCF values Ford at $16.23 against about $11 current. Call: F BUY first tracked at about $11, fair value $16.23. Bull: tariffs keep falling and F-150 ICE demand stays strong. Bear: margins stay near 2% and tariffs persist.

calls.thesis: BUY first tracked. Ford is a buying opportunity at ~$11: forward P/E of just 6, Wall Street forecasts 28% EPS growth over the next several years, and policy has turned in Ford's favour (EV mandate scrapped, tariffs easing). Operating margin is only 1.8% and autos are never very lucrative, but the valuation more than reflects that.
calls.base_case: Margins recover to low-to-mid single digits as Ford refocuses on ICE models like the F-150; average selling prices keep rising.
calls.bull_case: Tariffs keep falling (Supreme Court rulings, friendlier Canada relations) and F-150 ICE demand stays strong.
calls.bear_case: Margins stay near 2% and tariffs persist, capping returns despite the cheap multiple.
